quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases your chances of hitting road hazards and lets others pass.
Reduces your chances of hitting road hazards but lets you follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Choose a position that gives you the most space around you.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts occur between motorcycles and other vehicles. Riders should be extra careful when approaching and crossing intersections.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in:

options.text: The left side of your lane.
The center of your lane.
The right side of your lane.
Either the right or center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself on the left side of your lane before passing. This gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Brake harder than usual.
Brake more gently than usual.
Not use the rear brake.
Not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use caution and brake gently.

questions.question: Before riding, check everything except:

options.text: Your tire pressure.
How much tread is on your tires.
How shiny your tires are.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How shiny your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of your tire sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: For a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to keep the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to keep the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using both brakes together makes stopping easier and safer, especially if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergency stops.
Should only be used on slippery roads.
Is weaker than the rear brake.
Is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use as long as you use it properly.

questions.question: When riding at night, do all of the following except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase the distance between you and other vehicles.
Decrease the distance between you and other vehicles.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease the distance between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther. Use your high beam, except when you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay next to the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot, and the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to get away from the other vehicle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. This means you need more space and time to stop completely.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, away from road hazards, and gives you escape routes. It should always help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left often.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay away from parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. Moving left gives you more distance and time to react.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should apply throttle and:

options.text: Always slow down.
Keep steady speed or speed up slowly.
Speed up quickly.
Ignore your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Apply throttle through a turn to stabilize your motorcycle. Keep your speed steady or speed up gradually.

questions.question: A passenger should never:

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the rider leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers must wear helmets and eye protection. They should lean with the rider and wear snug clothing so nothing catches on the motorcycle. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully extended.
Use arms to hold body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than you would during the day.
At the same speed as during the day.
Faster than you would during the day.
On the road shoulder so others can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: You will reduce injury risk by wearing all of the following, except:

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
Face or eye protection.
Ear buds.
Protective clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes, and durable gloves to protect yourself.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around you.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Make riding more dangerous.
Make riding safer.
Only affect riding if you drink at the same time.
Affect everyone the same way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make riding more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Many drugs—including over-the-counter medications, prescription medications, and illegal drugs—have side effects that can impair your riding ability.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is encouraged if traffic is heavy.
Is encouraged during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Is acceptable if the motorcyclist is comfortable with the move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases your motorcycle, downshift and slowly approach it. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not kick the dog.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely on your mirrors to show you all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull over safely and check your tires.
